_comment: Ledger of third-party facts the skill depends on (client config paths, timeouts, budgets, SDK/API shapes, CI runtimes). Each entry records WHERE the fact was read and WHEN. scripts/verify_docs_sync.py asserts: every subject in `required_subjects` has an entry, every entry has an https source and a valid date, every `affects` path exists, and entries older than `max_age_days` are ::warning in CI and FAIL under --strict-staleness (the weekly docs-currency workflow files an issue). Re-verify = re-read the source, update `fact` if it changed, bump `verified_on`, and fix the code/docs in `affects` — that is the whole institution (AGENTS §2 v3).

facts.subject: claude-code
facts.fact: `claude mcp add --transport http|sse|stdio --scope local|project|user -e KEY=V -- cmd`; `.mcp.json` supports ${VAR} / ${VAR:-default} and per-server `timeout` (ms); tool and property names 1–64 chars; MCP output capped by MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS (25000); idle stdio servers reaped after 30 min; plugin manifests may declare mcpServers as .mcpb paths and use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} / userConfig.

facts.subject: claude-desktop
facts.fact: claude_desktop_config.json under ~/Library/Application Support/Claude (macOS) / %APPDATA%\Claude (Windows); .mcpb bundles install via Settings → Extensions; GUI clients do not inherit the shell PATH (absolute `uv` path required).

facts.subject: codex
facts.fact: config.toml [mcp_servers.<name>]: startup_timeout_sec default 10, tool_timeout_sec default 60, `env` table sets vars, `env_vars` forwards Codex's own env (older Codex rejects unknown keys in the table — do not write env_vars); default env whitelist HOME LOGNAME PATH SHELL USER __CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING LANG LC_ALL TERM TMPDIR TZ; Codex 0.158.0 (2026-09-28) added tool_input_schema_max_bytes default 5000 (oversize inputSchema is compacted: descriptions stripped) and startup_readiness = "catalog".

facts.subject: cursor
facts.fact: ~/.cursor/mcp.json (global) and .cursor/mcp.json (project); placeholders ${workspaceFolder} ${workspaceFolderBasename} ${env:X} ${userHome} ${pathSeparator}; deep link cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=&config=base64; docs table lists `type` (stdio) though examples omit it; ~40-tool practical cap (older observation, not on the docs page).

facts.subject: vscode
facts.fact: .vscode/mcp.json root key `servers`, `type` required, placeholders ${workspaceFolder} ${env:X} ${userHome} ${input:id}; new sandbox fields; 128-tool ceiling shared across servers (Copilot).

facts.subject: zed
facts.fact: settings.json `context_servers.<name>` = {command, args (optional since 2026-06), env, timeout (seconds, default 60)}; no `source` field; global context_server_timeout 60.

facts.subject: gemini
facts.fact: ~/.gemini/settings.json and project .gemini/settings.json `mcpServers`; per-server `timeout` in ms (default 600000), `trust` default false; tool FQN is unconditionally mcp_{serverName}_{toolName}, names over 63 chars are middle-truncated; $schema/additionalProperties stripped from schemas.

facts.subject: windsurf
facts.fact: Windsurf was renamed Devin Desktop on 2026-06-02; Cascade was removed in v3.9.19 (2026-09-08) and Devin Local is the only agent. It reads the Devin CLI MCP files: ~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json (macOS/Linux), %APPDATA%\devin\mcp_config.json (Windows), project .devin/mcp_config.json (+ .devin/mcp_config.local.json); root key mcpServers; stdio fields command/args/env/disabled; no per-server timeout. Legacy Cascade read ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json with a 100-tool cap. UNVERIFIED: whether Devin Local still reads the legacy `.windsurf/rules/*.md` rules files — the repo keeps that mirror until a Devin rules path is documented.

facts.subject: cline
facts.fact: cline_mcp_settings.json under the host editor's globalStorage/saoudrizwan.claude-dev/settings/; per-server `timeout` in seconds, default 60, range 1–3600; `type: stdio`; CLI also reads ~/.cline/mcp.json.

facts.subject: openclaw
facts.fact: OpenClaw consumes MCP through mcporter (npm, 0.9.0): `mcporter call <server>.<tool> --config <mcporter.json> --timeout <ms>`; first `npx mcporter` run downloads the package plus a native rolldown binding (~2 min on Windows runners); `mcporter` may hang after printing a result when a child server keeps stdio open (docs/hang-debug.md); MCPORTER_DEBUG_HANG=1 dumps handles.

facts.subject: remote-connectors
facts.fact: claude.ai custom connectors accept only OAuth (client id/secret), no static Bearer; ChatGPT remote MCP requires OAuth (CIMD; DCR still supported when configured) and search/fetch tools for deep research. The skill offers a static Bearer over streamable-http, so both need an OAuth-terminating HTTPS gateway.

facts.subject: mcp-python-sdk
facts.fact: Latest 1.x is 1.30.0 (2026-09-07): `streamablehttp_client(url, headers=…)` deprecated in favour of `streamable_http_client(url, http_client=httpx.AsyncClient)`; pydantic >= 2.11; idle streamable-http sessions closed after 30 min (session_idle_timeout), 10000-session cap; LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION 2025-11-25 while the spec's latest revision is 2026-07-28.

facts.subject: mcpb
facts.fact: @anthropic-ai/mcpb latest 2.1.2 (2025-12-04); manifest_version 0.4 with `uv` server type, optional privacy_policies / compatibility / user_config; `npx mcpb validate` + `mcpb pack`; packing is not byte-reproducible (sha must come from the uploaded build).

facts.subject: github-actions
facts.fact: Node 20 was removed from GitHub-hosted runners on 2026-09-23; JavaScript actions run on Node 24 and the ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION opt-out is gone. Node-24 majors used here: checkout v5, setup-python v6, setup-node v5, upload-artifact v6, download-artifact v7, cache v5, astral-sh/setup-uv v7, attest-build-provenance v3, codeql-action v4, dependency-review-action v5. Avoid download-artifact v8 (no auto-unzip, digest mismatch errors) and setup-uv v10 (cache disabled on release/pull_request_target/workflow_run) until validated on a draft matrix.

facts.subject: github-runner-images
facts.fact: macos-latest = macOS 26 arm64 (default Python 3.14, cached 3.12); windows-latest = windows-2025 (Python 3.12.10, Node 22, pwsh 7.6); windows-11-arm re-imaged 2026-09-21..30 (default Node 24 / Python 3.13, cached 3.12.10, no uv); ubuntu-latest moves to 26.04 in 2026-11. The workflows pin Python 3.12 and Node 22 explicitly.

facts.subject: uv
facts.fact: uv 0.12.14–0.12.20 (2026-09): no semantic change to `uvx --from <wheel URL|path>`; direct-URL dependencies are cached by URL and re-validated per HTTP cache headers (hence the local wheel cache in ~/.horosa/wheels/); 0.12.16 hash-verifies downloads; Windows MAX_PATH fix in 0.12.14.

facts.subject: node
facts.fact: Node 22 is Maintenance LTS until 2027-04-30 (payload ships the latest-v22.x line); Node 24 Active LTS; Node 26 enters LTS on 2026-10-28.

facts.subject: python
facts.fact: Python 3.12 is the runtime floor (requires-python >= 3.12) and the embedded payload interpreter; 3.13 is the default on the new windows-11-arm image, so workflows pin 3.12 explicitly.

facts.subject: swisseph
facts.fact: Swiss Ephemeris (libswe, built into pyswisseph) declares all of its state (ephemeris path, open files, sidereal mode) TLS: sweodef.h defines TLS as __thread (GCC) / __declspec(thread) (MSVC) unless __APPLE__, WIN32, DOS32 or TLSOFF is defined. A setuptools/MSVC build only has _WIN32, so on Windows swe_set_ephe_path applies to the calling thread only; on macOS the state is process-wide. Upstream v3.11.2's HOROSA_EPHE_PATH_FASTPATH caches 'path set' process-wide, so the Windows launcher turns it off (verified on windows-latest + windows-11-arm, diag runs 36802700937 / 36803364178). A thread that never set a path resolves one on first use through swe_set_ephe_path(NULL): the SE_EPHE_PATH environment variable comes first (it even beats an explicit set_ephe_path argument - verified 2026-10-01: SE_EPHE_PATH=C:\sweph\ephe made an explicit set_ephe_path(<bundled>) read C:\sweph\ephe\seas_18.se1), otherwise the compiled-in default '\sweph\ephe\' on the current drive: on a clean machine planets drop to Moshier and asteroids fail; where another astrology program left files there (maintainer box: C:\sweph\ephe, 2001-2014) the thread silently reads those (Chiron 0.14 arcsec off). Upstream astroextra calls swisseph without flatlib's ensureEphePath, so the Windows launcher also exports SE_EPHE_PATH=<bundled swefiles>, as the upstream desktop launcher does: published v0.40.0 cold start, 39 of 40 ephemeris responses off the bundled reference before, 40 of 40 identical after.

facts.subject: mcp-registry
facts.fact: Official MCP Registry (preview; schema 2025-12-11; mcp-publisher 1.8.1 = production 1.8.1). GitHub OIDC grants exactly `io.github.<repository_owner>/*` with GitHub's casing and the permission check is a case-sensitive prefix match (issue #689) → our name must be `io.github.Horace-Maxwell/horosa-skill`. mcpb packages: fileSha256 required (registry does not download/verify it; clients do), identifier must be an https github.com/gitlab.com tag-pinned `releases/download/<tag>/<file>` URL containing 'mcp' (`releases/latest/download` rejected), package `version` optional; publish HEADs the asset (200 or 3xx+Location, no redirect following) so a draft asset 404s. pypi packages must exist with an `mcp-name:` README marker. `_meta…/publisher-provided` ≤ 4096 bytes, other _meta keys dropped; description ≤ 100 chars; versions immutable (republish fails). `/v0/validate` and `mcp-publisher validate` check schema + semantics only (said valid:true for our old pypi+mcpb file). Probe: GET /v0.1/servers/<urlencoded name>/versions/<v> → 200 {server, _meta} when listed.

facts.subject: agent-plugins
facts.fact: Agent Plugins 1.0.0 (agent-plugins.org; 1.1.0 is a working draft whose schema URL 404s; Codex / VS Code / OpenHands hard-code 1.0.0). Root `plugin.json` with closed keys {$schema, name, version, description, author{name,email,url}, homepage, repository, license, keywords, extensions}; skills discovered as immediate children of `skills/`; MCP only in root `mcp.json` = {$schema, mcpServers}, stdio entries closed {type (required), command (single executable token, no placeholder expansion), args, env, cwd}; only ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/${PLUGIN_DATA} in args/env/cwd — Cursor does not expand them. No portable userConfig/secrets. Clients: VS Code, Copilot CLI (`copilot plugin install owner/repo`), Cursor, Codex (`codex plugin marketplace add owner/repo`), Kiro, OpenClaw, Hermes, OpenHands, NanoClaw, Grok Bot; Qwen Code documents support. VS Code / Copilot CLI / Codex / OpenHands prefer the root manifest over `.claude-plugin/`; OpenClaw and Claude Code keep the Claude format — no client loads both.

facts.subject: opencode
facts.fact: OpenCode v1.19.0: user file ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/opencode/opencode.json[c] (XDG layout on Windows too); JSONC; root `mcp`; stdio entry {type:'local', command:[program, ...args] (ONE array, no `args` key), environment (not env), enabled, timeout ms}; connect/list default 30 s in code (docs say 5 s), calls fall back to the SDK 60 s → write timeout 600000. No tool cap or deferral. Skills: reads ~/.agents/skills, ~/.claude/skills, ~/.config/opencode/skills. Verify: `opencode mcp list`.

facts.subject: goose
facts.fact: Goose v1.54.0: user file ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/goose/config.yaml on macOS/Linux, %APPDATA%\Block\goose\config\config.yaml on Windows, GOOSE_PATH_ROOT overrides; YAML holding all settings; root `extensions`; entry {enabled (required), type:stdio, name, cmd, args (required), envs, env_keys, timeout SECONDS (default 300, fixed wall clock per request)}; a malformed entry is skipped silently. Skills: ~/.agents/skills is the canonical writable folder. Verify: `goose info -v`.

facts.subject: kiro
facts.fact: Kiro (IDE + CLI): user file ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json (KIRO_HOME overrides; Windows path inferred); root mcpServers {command,args,env,disabled}; no timeout field documented for mcp.json; Kiro CLI global mcp.initTimeout defaults to 5000 ms (45 s cold start exceeds it → tell the user `kiro-cli settings mcp.initTimeout 120000`). Skills: ~/.kiro/skills only (no ~/.agents documented). Confidence medium.

facts.subject: copilot-cli
facts.fact: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.95: user file ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json (COPILOT_HOME overrides); root mcpServers {type:'local'|'stdio', command, args, env, tools (listed required → ['*']), timeout ms (discovery + calls, default 30000; connection floored at 60 s)}; docs: 'The PATH variable is automatically inherited … All other environment variables must be configured here' (not checked in source) → write HOME/USERPROFILE + runtime roots, probe with PATH only. Project .mcp.json is shared with Claude Code (never written). Skills: ~/.agents/skills unless COPILOT_HOME is set (then $COPILOT_HOME/skills).

facts.subject: junie
facts.fact: JetBrains Junie CLI: user file ~/.junie/mcp/mcp.json (Windows path and JUNIE_HOME effect inferred); root mcpServers {command,args,env}; no timeout fields documented (write none). Its MCP installation assistant searches the official MCP Registry. Skills: ~/.junie/skills and ~/.agents/skills. Confidence medium.

facts.subject: qwen
facts.fact: Qwen Code v0.25.1: user file ~/.qwen/settings.json (QWEN_HOME overrides); JSON with comments (no trailing commas), holds all settings; root mcpServers {command,args,env,discoveryTimeoutMs (connect+list, default 30000 stdio, 100..300000), timeout (tool call, default 600000)}; top-level mcp.allowed / mcp.excluded filter servers. Skills: ~/.qwen/skills and ~/.agents/skills (source).

facts.subject: kimi
facts.fact: Kimi Code CLI 2.1.1: user file ~/.kimi-code/mcp.json (KIMI_CODE_HOME overrides); strict JSON — ONE invalid entry fails the whole file; root mcpServers {command,args,env,startupTimeoutMs (default 30000), toolTimeoutMs (SDK default 60000)}; no `type` (transport inferred). Skills: ~/.kimi-code/skills and ~/.agents/skills; a loose .md in a skills root registers as a skill.

facts.subject: qoder
facts.fact: Qoder CLI / new desktop app: user file ~/.qoder/settings.json (QODER_CONFIG_DIR overrides; Windows inferred); JSON with // comments, holds every CLI setting; root mcpServers {command,args,env,timeout ms (connection + request)}; the older Qoder IDE configures MCP only in its UI. Skills: ~/.qoder/skills (~/.agents/skills home vs project undocumented). Confidence medium.

facts.subject: codebuddy
facts.fact: Tencent CodeBuddy Code: USER scope reads ONLY the first existing of ~/.codebuddy/.mcp.json, ~/.codebuddy/mcp.json (deprecated), ~/.codebuddy.json (legacy), never merged (CODEBUDDY_CONFIG_DIR replaces ~/.codebuddy); JSONC; root mcpServers {type:'stdio', command, args, env}; timeouts only via process env MCP_TIMEOUT / MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT; over ~30 tools → deferred loading; output cap MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS 20000. Skills: ~/.codebuddy/skills. Confidence medium (docs contradict on `type` and deferral).

facts.subject: trae
facts.fact: TRAE IDE: NO documented user-level file — Settings > MCP > Add > Create Manually, or deep link trae://trae.ai-ide/mcp-import?type=stdio&name=<n>&config=<urlencoded base64 of the entry JSON> (Trae CN: trae-cn://); project .trae/mcp.json only after 'Enable Project MCP'; entry {command,args,env}; timeouts as env strings START_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS / RUN_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS; command must not contain spaces; HARD caps across all servers: 40 tools, 8000 description chars. Skills: ~/.trae/skills (~/.trae-cn/skills for Trae CN).

facts.subject: amp
facts.fact: Amp: user file ~/.config/amp/settings.json (or .jsonc; JSONC); the root key is the LITERAL top-level string "amp.mcpServers" (a nested amp:{mcpServers} is invalid); stdio entry {command,args,env} with additionalProperties:false — no timeout or other keys. Skills: reads ~/.agents/skills, ~/.config/amp/skills, ~/.claude/skills. Verify: `amp mcp doctor`.

facts.subject: warp
facts.fact: Warp: user file ~/.warp/.mcp.json on every OS (%USERPROFILE%\.warp\.mcp.json; Warp deliberately avoids XDG/AppData); strict JSON; root mcpServers {command,args,env}; no timeout field (tool calls hard-coded 30 min); auto-detects saves. Optional auto-spawn of Claude Code / Codex servers can duplicate an entry. Skills: ~/.agents/skills (recommended by Warp).

facts.subject: droid
facts.fact: Factory Droid: user file ~/.factory/mcp.json; root mcpServers {type:'stdio', command, args, env, connectTimeout ms (stdio default 30000), timeout ms (tool call), disabled}; reloads on change. Skills: ~/.factory/skills, ~/.agents/skills — duplicate names in one bucket are invalid configuration (install one copy).

facts.subject: augment
facts.fact: Augment Auggie CLI 0.36.0: user file ~/.augment/settings.json (JSONC, comments preserved by its own writes); root mcpServers {type:'stdio', command, args, env}; no documented timeout keys (bundle: host init waits 15 s then proceeds; calls 600 s between progress, 1800 s total; a 30 s liveness ping during calls). The IDE extensions use their own settings panel. Skills: ~/.augment/skills, ~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills.

facts.subject: deepcode
facts.fact: Deep Code 0.4.3 (recommended in DeepSeek API docs): user file ~/.deepcode/settings.json shared with its VS Code extension; STRICT JSON — JSON.parse with catch→null drops the WHOLE file (API key included) on one comment or trailing comma; root mcpServers {command,args,env} only; startup DEEPCODE_MCP_TIMEOUT process env (default 30000); tool calls FIXED at 60000 ms (not configurable). Skills: ~/.deepcode/skills, ~/.agents/skills.

facts.subject: dsh
facts.fact: DeepSeek Harness 0.2.0-rc.2 (developer preview, breaking changes promised): config ~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml (DSH_HOME) is a YAML LIST of Cordis patch ops that may hold other user patches and !!js tags — do not edit it; ship a standalone patch [{insert:[{id, name:'@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client', config:{serverName, transport:'stdio', command, args, env, toolCallTimeoutMs (default 60000)}}]}] used via `dsh web --patch <file>`; server instructions over 32 KiB are rejected. Skills: ~/.dsh/skills and ~/.agents/skills ($DSH_AGENTS_HOME).

facts.subject: agent-skills
facts.fact: User-level Agent Skills folders, 2026-10-12: ~/.agents/skills is read by Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Codex (the documented USER location; $CODEX_HOME/skills deprecated), Gemini CLI (alias, GEMINI_CLI_HOME relocates), Devin Desktop / Windsurf, Cline, Zed (ONLY there), OpenCode, Goose, Junie, Qwen Code, Kimi Code, Amp, Warp, Droid, Augment, Deep Code, dsh, and Copilot CLI unless COPILOT_HOME is set. Own folder only: Claude Code ~/.claude/skills ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills), Kiro ~/.kiro/skills, Qoder ~/.qoder/skills, CodeBuddy ~/.codebuddy/skills, TRAE ~/.trae/skills. Claude Desktop chat/Cowork take skills only as an uploaded ZIP. Cursor / VS Code / Codex also read ~/.claude/skills, so a copy in both folders is listed twice; Droid treats a duplicate name in one bucket as invalid configuration.

facts.subject: opencc
facts.fact: OpenCC 1.4.2 (PyPI `opencc`, uploaded 2026-08-22, Apache-2.0) ships wheels for macOS x86_64/arm64, manylinux x86_64/aarch64 and win_amd64 only — no win_arm64, so installing it on Windows ARM falls back to a C++ sdist build. Its s2tw / s2hk configs are: normalize CJK compatibility ideographs → mmseg segmentation on STPhrases → (STPhrases ∪ generated regional phrases, then STCharacters) → (TW|HK VariantsPhrases, then Variants). Horosa bundles the text dictionaries instead of the package; without the Horosa term table its longest-match converter equals official s2tw/s2hk on 2 072 209 characters of real output (2026-10-22).

facts.subject: mcpb
facts.fact: MCPB manifest user_config types are string / number / boolean (checkbox) / directory / file, referenced as ${user_config.KEY} in env; the spec does not state the string form a boolean takes when substituted, so a boolean setting must be parsed leniently (true/false, 1/0, on/off, yes/no).

facts.subject: claude-code
facts.fact: Claude Code plugin.json userConfig options are strict objects (unknown key = plugin fails to load) with type string / number / boolean / directory / file; `options` (a fixed picker for string fields) needs Claude Code v2.1.271+ and older versions cannot load a plugin that declares it, so Horosa uses a boolean for the Traditional-output switch.

facts.subject: windows
facts.fact: Windows 11 Smart App Control blocks apps that are unsigned and whose cloud reputation is unknown (state in HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CI\Policy VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState: 0 off / 1 on / 2 evaluation); a blocked spawn surfaces as os error 4551 (ERROR_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY_POLICY_VIOLATION). uv/uvx per-environment Scripts\*.exe trampolines can be blocked while the interpreter's own python.exe is not. Recent Windows updates let users re-enable it from Windows Security without a clean install. The decision is cached per file instance and re-evaluated: an identical-hash unsigned .pyd (astropy 7.2.0 time/_parse_times.pyd) loaded in one runtime root and was refused (DLL load failed: An Application Control policy has blocked this file) in a freshly installed one.
